narrative: OMX30 enters Tuesday in a structurally bullish regime (+8.2% vs 200-MA, ADX 41.1 strong) but faces near-term mean-reversion headwinds. The MACD bearish crossover and RSI at 69.72 flag overbought conditions despite positive momentum (ROC-90 +11.8%). Global correlation is slightly negative (-0.040%), with mixed European opens (DAX +0.53% but CAC/FTSE lower) and weakness across US/Asia overnight. The sharp US 10Y yield spike (+119bps to 4.696%) creates a bifurcated setup: banks should benefit from wider NIM, but tech, real estate, and high-multiple sectors face DCF compression. USD/SEK strength (+0.12%) supports Swedish exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson), partially offsetting NASDAQ weakness (-0.28%). Asymmetric risk: upside capped by overbought technicals and yield headwinds; downside accelerates if VIX (currently 14.25, -2.60%) reverts or geopolitical (Trump/Korea) escalates.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected to open marginally higher into overbought conditions. DAX strength (+0.53%) provides modest tailwind, but MACD bearish crossover, RSI 69.72, and -1.6% distance from 52W high all warn of pullback risk—watch 3123 pivot (yesterday close) and lower Bollinger support at 3085 as critical holds. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) are primary beneficiaries of the yield spike to 4.696%, likely outperforming industrials/tech today. Exporters (Volvo B, Atlas Copco A, Ericsson B) supported by USD/SEK +0.12%, but NASDAQ weakness (-0.28%) and AI sentiment headwinds (FT: 'AI hasn't gone rogue. It's worse than that') could cap Hexagon and Ericsson gains. Boliden and mining names should be on watch—gold +0.59% and Brent +0.91% are modest tailwinds, though copper -0.49% is a small headwind. Key intraday catalyst: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET (could reignite yield volatility). Trade recommendation: play the bank outperformance early, trim into any bounce above 3140, and avoid chasing into overbought tech.
